title: Denis Villeneuve Defends Casting Robert Pattinson as Bond: ‘We Will Never Please Everybody’
summary: "At the end of the day, the truth will be on the screen," the filmmaker says The post Denis Villeneuve Defends Casting Robert Pattinson as Bond: ‘We Will Never Please Everybody’ appeared first on TheWrap .
content: Denis Villeneuve has addressed the inevitable criticism of his choice to cast Robert Pattinson as James Bond , noting on Friday, “No matter what we do, we will never please everybody.” Villeneuve spoke extensively about his newest film, “Dune: Part Three,” as well as his untitled Bond project, in a new interview with Time Magazine . While the interview was conducted prior to Pattinson’s reveal as 007 , Villeneuve predicted there would be a “hurricane” of responses to his decision once it was publicly announced. “When Daniel Craig was cast, it was a s—tstorm. He was blond. He was short. He was not seen as an action hero,” Villeneuve observed. “Yet when we talk about James Bond today it is because of Daniel Craig’s extraordinary interpretation. And that was a different environment in 2006 before social media.” “I expect a hurricane when we bring our choice to the world. Some people will be happy. Some will be mad. I can do nothing about that,” he added. “At the end of the day, the truth will be on the screen. Then they will be able to judge.” Villeneuve also shrugged off a question about the betting markets that had sprouted up in the months preceding his pivotal casting decision. “I read nothing about that. My responsibility is to make the best casting and create the best story for that cast. I cannot listen to the rumors,” he said. “No matter what we do, we will never please everybody.” In the same interview, Villeneuve said he felt like he has “electricity in my veins” ideating about his Bond film, which will be his first project not set in the “Dune” universe since 2017’s “Blade Runner 2049.” He went on to offer some brief insight into what Bond fans should expect from his forthcoming reboot. “I will say: I love traditions. I love the unapologetic way the character behaves, the panache,” Villeneuve said. “I’m not here to change the DNA of James Bond. I’m here to embrace it, to bring it to the world of today.” “I’m a hardcore James Bond fan, and I want other fans to have fun watching my film,” he continued. “Of course, it will be tainted by my sensibility. But I wake up every morning with a stupid smile because it’s a world of pure cinematic pleasure.” Little is known right now about Villeneuve’s Bond project outside of Pattinson’s casting. “Peaky Blinders” creator Steven Knight has been tapped to write the script for the film, which will be the first Bond movie since Craig concluded his acclaimed run as the character in 2021’s “No Time to Die.” The post Denis Villeneuve Defends Casting Robert Pattinson as Bond: ‘We Will Never Please Everybody’ appeared first on TheWrap .

title: Amy Poehler and Tina Fey Roast LA Thanksgivings
summary: Of course they use their best Valley girl voices to do it The post Amy Poehler and Tina Fey Roast LA Thanksgivings appeared first on TheWrap .
content: Depending on where in the country you live, Thanksgiving probably looks pretty different to other people’s. So, on Thursday night, Amy Poehler and Tina Fey took some time out to roast LA Thanksgivings in particular. Both women were guests on Seth Meyers’ Thanksgiving episode of “Late Night,” and early on in the interview, admitted that their Thanksgivings have two very different vibes. Fey, being a New Yorker, described a holiday that tests your fortitude just a bit. “New York Thanksgiving, you get up, you stand in the ice cold wind, you look at giant balloons that hopefully are — the wind is blowing them into a sexual position you can laugh about,” Fey detailed. “Go home. You trip on a rat. You have a nice meal.” With that, Poehler began describing an average Thanksgiving in Los Angeles, putting on her best Valley girl voice. “In LA, we do things a little differently,” she joked. “We have turkey, or a turkey substitute, and then we get a smoothie, and then we eat our leftovers on the beach. And it’s different. But it’s fun!” Naturally, Fey immediately joined in on the joke, putting on her own affected voice, and taking the bit even further. “You put all your sides and your turkey in the bowl, and shake it like a salad,” Fey joked. “And then you go, ‘Mm mm mm,’ and you don’t eat it!” Not one to be left out, Meyers also joined in on the joke, though unfortunately, he didn’t use a funny voice to do it. title: Justin Timberlake Refuses to Sing Backstreet Boys Song During ‘Tonight Show’ Mash-Up: ‘Sacrilegious!’
summary: "I do not desire this!" the NSYNC singer protests The post Justin Timberlake Refuses to Sing Backstreet Boys Song During ‘Tonight Show’ Mash-Up: ‘Sacrilegious!’ appeared first on TheWrap .
content: If you were a pop music fan in the early 2000s (particularly if you’re a woman), you likely had some very heated arguments with your friends on one topic in particular: Backstreet Boys vs. NSYNC. You had to be one or the other, and on Thursday night, Justin Timberlake made his allegiances pretty clear. Obviously, he’ll always be Team NSYNC considering, well, he was in the band. But when it came time to actually perform a Backstreet Boys song during his Thanksgiving appearance on “The Tonight Show,” Timberlake jokingly refused. “Oh god,” he said as the music kicked in. “No, no, no, no, no, no, no.” Host Jimmy Fallon took the lead, having no qualms about musically betraying his best friend. As Fallon sang the opening lyrics of “I Want It That Way,” Timberlake ripped his hand from Fallon’s. “I do not desire this!” he said. Still, Fallon pressed on, singing earnestly. “This is sacrilegious, what will the fans say?” Timberlake tried one last time, before happily singing out with his whole chest. Naturally, the audience joined in as well. The number was part of the duo’s “History of Party Songs” bit, in which they sang a roughly 6-minute mashup of popular party songs from over the years, including “This Is How We Do It,” “Brick House,” “Get Low” and more. Surprisingly (and perhaps insultingly), and for reasons unknown, no NSYNC songs made it into the medley of party songs. title: BBC Faces Antisemitism Investigation Over Treatment of Jewish Staff
summary: Britain’s independent antisemitism adviser will examine whether employees’ complaints point to a wider institutional problem The post BBC Faces Antisemitism Investigation Over Treatment of Jewish Staff appeared first on TheWrap .
content: The BBC is facing an independent investigation into allegations of antisemitism in its workplace, raising questions about whether one of the world’s most prominent public broadcasters is adequately addressing the concerns of its Jewish employees. Lord John Mann, the British government’s independent adviser on antisemitism, announced Thursday that he was launching the investigation after hearing from Jewish BBC staffers, some of whom he said were afraid to raise concerns about discrimination internally. The investigation comes weeks after a senior BBC executive said there was no evidence of systemic discrimination that would warrant an independent inquiry. It also comes at a sensitive time for the broadcaster, as the British government reviews its governance, funding and public service obligations ahead of the expiration of its Royal Charter at the end of 2027. Mann told BBC Radio 4’s “Today” program Thursday that previous efforts by the corporation to address employees’ concerns had been unsuccessful. His investigation will seek to establish whether the complaints reflect isolated incidents or a broader institutional problem. In a speech Thursday evening, Mann said his decision to intervene stemmed from his belief in the BBC’s future. He argued that marginalizing the voices and perspectives of Jewish employees was incompatible with fair and independent broadcasting. The BBC said in a statement that it takes “any and all allegations of discrimination extremely seriously – there is no place for it at the BBC.” The broadcaster has introduced mandatory antisemitism training for all employees and encourages staffers to report incidents of discrimination. Earlier this month, BBC Deputy Director General Rhodri Talfan Davies met with representatives of the broadcaster’s Jewish staff network. He also defended the corporation’s existing procedures for handling discrimination complaints, saying they were robust and regularly reviewed, according to The Guardian . The BBC did not immediately respond to TheWrap’s request for comment on whether it intends to cooperate with Mann’s investigation. The meeting followed revelations by Oscar-winning documentary producer Lucie Kon that she had received a £400,000 ($523,852) payout from the BBC after raising allegations of antisemitism. The BBC said it had not upheld Kon’s allegations of antisemitism but acknowledged shortcomings in its treatment of her. Speaking at an event in Manchester on Thursday evening, Mann urged current and former BBC employees to come forward, emphasizing that his investigation was intended to strengthen the broadcaster, Jewish News reported Friday . “What I am repeatedly hearing is people feel cowed and intimidated and frightened, and stay silent and suffer in silence,” he said. Mann has guaranteed anonymity to those who contact him and expects to present his findings to the BBC and the government before Easter. Britain’s Department for Culture, Media and Sport said it would carefully consider Mann’s findings, emphasizing the BBC’s responsibility to ensure that all communities are represented and valued in British public life. The workplace investigation is among several challenges facing the broadcaster. Separately, the BBC is fighting President Donald Trump’s $10 billion defamation lawsuit over the editing of his Jan. 6, 2021, speech for a documentary. The corporation has asked a U.S. federal appeals court to intervene , arguing that the Florida court overseeing the case lacks jurisdiction. title: UK Backs Bill to Protect Journalists From Abusive Lawsuits
summary: Press freedom advocates say the proposed safeguards don't go far enough The post UK Backs Bill to Protect Journalists From Abusive Lawsuits appeared first on TheWrap .
content: The British government on Friday backed legislation aimed at preventing wealthy individuals and organizations from using costly lawsuits to intimidate journalists and suppress investigative reporting. The bill would expand legal protections for journalists and whistleblowers in England and Wales beyond cases involving economic crime. However, press freedom advocates warn that reporters could still incur substantial legal expenses before qualifying for those protections. Existing safeguards against strategic lawsuits against public participation, commonly known as SLAPPs, were introduced in 2023. The new legislation would extend those measures to investigations into sexual misconduct and other matters of public interest. Similar concerns exist in the U.S., where 40 states and Washington, D.C., had enacted anti-SLAPP legislation as of August, but no equivalent federal law exists . “No one should be able to use their wealth or influence to silence legitimate scrutiny,” Sarah Sackman, Britain’s minister for courts and legal services, said in a statement Friday. Under the legislation, judges could dismiss lawsuits identified as SLAPPs early in proceedings if plaintiffs cannot demonstrate that their claims are likely to succeed. Defendants would also generally be shielded from paying plaintiffs’ legal costs in such cases, even if they lose. The UK Anti-SLAPP Coalition has called for changes to the bill, arguing that its early dismissal mechanism is too complicated and sets too high a legal threshold, according to a House of Commons research briefing published Wednesday. “At present, the early dismissal process in the Bill is incredibly complex,” National Union of Journalists General Secretary Laura Davison said in a statement Monday. The British government’s announcement comes amid an ongoing legal battle between the BBC and President Trump in the U.S. The broadcaster recently asked a federal appeals court to toss Trump’s defamation lawsuit over its editing of his Jan. 6, 2021, speech. The bill, introduced by Conservative lawmaker John Whittingdale, received its second reading in the House of Commons Friday and must clear further legislative stages before becoming law.
